t: The provisions under the heading “civil service retirement and disability fund” in title I of the Independent Offices Appropriation Act, 1959 (72 Stat. 1064; Public Law 85–844), shall not apply with respect to benefits resulting from the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only exempts benefits under this Act from an appropriations provision on the civil service retirement and disability fund. There is no tempting reading: no outside party is consulted, heard, placed on a committee, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is authorized. It is a purely internal funding and benefits rule.
fable.s: shall not apply with respect to benefits resulting from the enactment of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical provision regarding the applicability of funding sources for civil service retirement benefits. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. It merely defines which statutory provisions apply to specific benefits.
qwen_block.s: The provisions under the heading “civil service retirement and disability fund” in title I of the Independent Offices Appropriation Act, 1959 (72 Stat. 1064; Public Law 85–844), shall not apply with respect to benefits resulting from the enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This section only says that an earlier appropriations provision on the civil service retirement fund does not apply to benefits created by this Act. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in a decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The word "benefits" does not make it participation, and the definition excludes benefits matters anyway.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** Someone might read "benefits" or "civil service" as a sign of a process involving people. That reading fails. The section only says that an earlier appropriations provision does not apply to benefits created by this Act. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, given a comment period, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a fiscal provision that excludes a specific fund from applying to certain benefits. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There is no advisory board, public hearing, comment period, or right to sue mentioned. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The provisions under the heading “civil service retirement and disability fund” in title I of the Independent Offices Appropriation Act, 1959 (72 Stat. 1064; Public Law 85–844), shall not apply with respect to benefits resulting from the enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section mentions "benefits," it relates to applications for benefits, which are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. However, the section does not describe an application process or any interaction with outside parties; it merely excludes a specific funding source from applying to certain benefits.
